youtube.title: The Sage's Sister Who Became a River | Ramayana Ep 9
youtube.description:
Vishvamitra's own sister became a river. 🌊

That night, camped on the bank of the Shona, the sage told Rama about his elder sister, Satyavati, who was given in marriage to Richika. Holy, steadfast in truth and dharma, and true to her husband, she followed him to heaven in her own body. Then she flowed forth as the Kaushiki, a holy river on the Himalaya, for the good of the world. So the sage made his home beside her on the Himalayan slopes, out of love. Only his vow drew him away to Siddhashrama, a vow, he said, that Rama's splendour had fulfilled. Past midnight, he bade Rama sleep, so that nothing would hinder their road. Around them the trees stood still, the birds lay hidden, and the cool moon rose. And Rama, a little wonderstruck, slept beside Lakshmana. At dawn they set out, and by midday they reached the Ganga, alive with swans and cranes. There Rama asked how this river crossed three worlds to reach the sea.

📜 On screen (Valmiki Ramayana 1.34.10, vulgate):
"Tato'haṃ himavatpārśve vasāmi niyataḥ sukham, bhaginyāṃ snehasaṃyuktaḥ kauśikyāṃ raghunandana"
(So, O joy of the Raghus, I live content and disciplined on the flank of the Himalaya, bound by love for my sister, the Kaushiki.)
